errors.english: Even if the vocal object [note: sound] does not by its very nature possess a variegated conjunction
errors.why: sgra'i yul is the referent of the word (śabdaviṣaya), here conjunction itself, and the clause says that conjunction is not variegated in nature, not that 'sound' lacks a variegated conjunction.

fix.find: Even if the vocal object [note: sound] does not by its very nature possess a variegated conjunction
fix.replace: Even if conjunction, the referent of the word ["variegated"], is not by its very nature variegated

note: A sound rendering of the argument against a variegated conjunction (saṃyoga) as the ground of citra-cognition, marred by one misreading of sgra'i yul with a wrong gloss.

errors.english: regarding the statement that being a speaker and being omniscient are impossible [note: original: "mi srid"], it is not impossible for both of those two aspects, being omniscient and being a speaker, to exist together.
errors.why: The lemma says contradiction is 'not possible in the case of speakerhood and omniscience', glossed as: neither of the two kinds of contradiction (just defined) can hold between omniscience and speakerhood; the English misreads the lemma and drops the two kinds of virodha.

fix.find: regarding the statement that being a speaker and being omniscient are impossible [note: original: "mi srid"], it is not impossible for both of those two aspects, being omniscient and being a speaker, to exist together.
fix.replace: regarding the words "not possible in the case of being a speaker and being omniscient": neither of those two kinds of contradiction is possible between being omniscient and being a speaker.

errors.english: we do not see any contradiction between them
errors.why: ldog pa here is the cessation of speech: when the causes of speech are complete, speech is not seen to cease when omniscience is present.

errors.english: the non-inference of a second entity
errors.why: mi dmigs pa is non-perception (anupalabdhi), not non-inference.

fix.find: the non-inference of a second entity
fix.replace: the non-perception of a second entity

errors.english: regarding the exclusion of passion and so forth in one who teaches
errors.why: ldan par ston pa means 'proving (someone) to be possessed of' passion etc. (the second inference, with speakerhood as reason), not 'one who teaches'.

fix.find: regarding the exclusion of passion and so forth in one who teaches
fix.replace: regarding exclusion in proving that someone possesses passion and so forth

note: The overall line of Dharmottara's sandigdhavyatireka discussion survives, but the opening gloss, the key term anupalabdhi and the framing of the second inference are misread.

errors.english: It should be given to the one who is close by.
errors.why: Nye ba 'khor is the name Upāli, addressed by the Buddha in the canonical answer: 'Upāli, it should be given.'

fix.find: It should be given to the one who is close by.

note: A careful rendering of a difficult Vinayasūtra commentary passage, except that the interlocutor Upāli is translated as 'the one close by'.

errors.english: when it is stated that a part of the subject's property that is to be proven is pervaded
errors.why: The formula (pakṣadharmas tadaṃśena vyāptaḥ) says the property of the subject is pervaded BY a part of the pakṣa, i.e. the property to be proven; the English makes the part the thing pervaded.

fix.find: when it is stated that a part of the subject's property that is to be proven is pervaded
fix.replace: when it is stated that the property of the subject of the probandum is pervaded by a part of the thesis (pakṣa)

errors.english: Since these are of an all-present nature, such a distinction is impossible.
errors.why: The two reasons are that anvaya/vyatireka consist in presence across all instances, and that such presence is impossible for a particular (the subject); the English makes the distinction itself impossible.

errors.english: it is appropriate that the qualifier itself functions as the means of understanding
errors.why: khyad par bya ba is the qualified (here the pervaded, the reason) as means of understanding the pervader, not the qualifier.

note: The commentary on the Hetubindu definition and the three eva-restrictions is followable, but the central pervasion formula has its case roles inverted and the pervader/pervaded relation is blurred in places.

errors.english: (Sanghadisesa) Formal Meeting of the Sangha, a major category of monastic offense
errors.why: This is the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya, so the Sanskrit saṅghāvaśeṣa (dge 'dun gyi lhag ma) is meant, not the Pali saṅghādisesa with its Pali-derived gloss.

fix.find: (Sanghadisesa) Formal Meeting of the Sangha, a major category of monastic offense

errors.why: The term is nyes byas = duṣkṛta; 'dus-kyas' is a garbled form.

errors.english: such as by looking at the form of a woman or other such objects to arouse passion
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks of seeing forms that arouse attachment; 'a woman' is not in the text.

note: The casuistry of the first saṅghāvaśeṣa (impulse, sheath, sleep emissions) is followed accurately; problems are a Pali offense name, a garbled duṣkṛta and unmarked inline glosses.
The colophon of the Śrīsena chapter and the opening verses of the next pallava are rendered faithfully from the Tibetan, with the Sanskrit context sensibly handled.
A faithful rendering of Prajñākaramati on the authenticity of the Mahāyāna, including the transmission lineage and the parity argument against the Vaibhāṣikas.

errors.english: She spoke thus to him, and the merchant's daughter replied: "Noble son, he will teach me
errors.why: It is Sadāprarudita who answers the merchant's daughter, addressing her as 'girl' (bu mo): that noble son will teach me the perfection of wisdom and skill in means.

fix.find: She spoke thus to him, and the merchant's daughter replied: "Noble son, he will teach me
fix.replace: He said to her: "Daughter, that noble son will teach me

errors.why: The bodhisattva's Sanskrit name is Sadāprarudita.

errors.english: all this should be applied extensively.
errors.why: The 'from ... up to ... apply in full' formula is Śāntideva's abridgement of the sūtra quotation, not part of the merchant's daughter's speech, and the later abridgement markers ('from ... up to') are dropped so the excerpt reads as continuous narrative.

note: The Sadāprarudita excerpt reads smoothly, but the speaker of the key reply is reversed and the compiler's abridgement formulas are merged into the sūtra speech.

errors.english: At the conclusion of the speech
errors.why: Completing the previous side, it says: when the sky-going gods' acclaim of the king ('well done!') spread to the ends of the quarters; 'conclusion of the speech' loses this.

errors.english: With a body cut despite its great fragrance
errors.why: The mango's body is cut because of its fragrance (Skt. saurabhacchinnatanu), not despite it.

note: The lament over the king who gave his body is rendered well overall, with two medium-confidence slips in the verse imagery.
A careful rendering of the subcommentary on why 'certainty' (niścita) is included in the definition of the triply characterised reason, with the anvaya/vyatireka argument correctly handled.
